column1: Each generation is a DISTINCT BUILD: it is produced by a
different compiler, and the compiler identity is recorded as a
G1, G2 and G3 are the SAME PolyC source compiled by THREE
DIFFERENT compilers.  Their component objects are byte-identical,
which is EXPECTED: the compiler is deterministic and the source is
identical.  What distinguishes them is the COMPILER, and the
G0 is an INTENTIONAL LEGACY REFERENCE.  It is built from C, so
byte-identity with the PolyC generations is NOT expected and is NOT
required.  The permitted G0-versus-PolyC comparison contract is
SEMANTIC (the oracle differential), and it is exercised below.
